title: Abelian counit comparisons and component normalization for coefficient squares
statement: For a site (C,J), commutative rings B and R, b:R→B, a ring sheaf T and a locally bijective presentation α:const(R)→T, define forgetIso from Res_b followed by module-presheaf realization and α-module sheafification, then forgetting to abelian sheaves, to the original underlying abelian sheaf. It is the associator, the abelian sheafification counit, and the right unitor. The fixed-ring and ring-sheaf scalar restriction comparisons are the identity on underlying abelian sheaves. For a square c and specified forgetful isomorphisms r,a,aprime,q, normalized(c,r,a,aprime,q) means equality of the two pasted natural transformations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Its component criterion is Hprime(c_X)≫r_FX≫a_X=aprime_QX≫q_X.

source.place: The module-sheafification adjunction, its forgetful hom-equivalence formulas and unit; the scalar-composition isomorphism of ModuleCat.

proof.text: Use the counit of abelian sheafification for forgetIso. Both scalar restriction comparisons are identity maps. Define normalized by the explicit pasted-transformation equality. For its component criterion, apply NatTrans.ext and function extensionality, expand only the abstract associator and whiskering components, and remove identity maps. All category and functor variables stay abstract in this calculation.
